correctness.rationale: The exact developed-sector intrinsic metric gives independent radial densities 2r and short azimuth separation uniform on [0,π]. Squared distance is radially convex; its only global maxima are tip–rim (distance 1) and opposite rim–rim (distance 2sin(πc/2)). Uniform localization near those orbits is valid by compactness. Positive first radial derivatives give ε³ near both orbits, with one vanishing radial sampling factor for tip–rim; explicit scaled simplex integrations yield 4tan(πc)/(3πc) and 2/(3πc cos(πc/2) sin²(πc/2)). At c=1/3 the orbits are disjoint and coefficients sum to 28/(π√3). For c=1 angular derivative vanishes, resulting in ε^(5/2) with coefficient 32/(15π). All computations are analytical with stated error/localization conditions. The standalone standard-library verifier independently checks sampling normalization, known exact moments, diameter candidates, and near-diameter quadratures in 67 comparisons.

value.rationale: The complete near-diameter random-pair distributional asymptotic on an intrinsically conical lateral surface measures the volume of nearly diametral pairs, a natural metric-measure invariant not determined by diameter or moments. Two competing geometrically distinct maximizer types produce an exact critical addition of coefficients, while angular degeneracy in the disk limit changes the exponent. Uniformity over all fixed nonflat cone opening parameters, with exact critical and flat-limit cases, is a complete natural phase classification beyond a routine single numerical example; no general-cone-surface theorem is asserted.
